subject: Post-call architectural worksheet + SDK sandbox next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@dataco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call architectural worksheet + SDK sandbox next steps

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and proposal so we have a single place to track the integration path and immediate next steps. I summarized the technical asks you mentioned and added recommended quickstart approaches: 

1) Goals we heard
- Evaluate Redwood SDK for inference routing (hosted vs. dedicated) and auth model for PII-sensitive workloads.
- Validate structured output / tool-calling support for your agent workflow (ticket creation + internal lookups).
- Test embeddings + reranker on a representative subset of your KB (~200k docs) for search relevance.

2) Recommended sandbox scope (2-week tech POC)
- Local dev: SDK installs for Python and TypeScript, run sample app that mimics your ticket routing flow.
- Auth: test API keys + temporary OAuth flow; in parallel validate that VPC/private deployment can accept your SAML assertions (if we get to dedicated).
- Routing: show request-based routing to cheaper model for background re-rank vs. low-latency model for interactive responses.
- Structured output/tool-calling: wire a simple tool (create_ticket) and demo invocation + verification.
- Embeddings/rerank: run small embedding pipeline and a reranker candidate set to show improvement over baseline.

3) Deliverables we propose
- Sandbox repo (Python + TS sample apps) + runbook (attached integration-worksheet.pdf)
- Mutual action plan with milestones (attached)
- 60–90 minute technical demo + live pairing session to run the sample app locally

4) Proposed timeline
- Week 1: SDK install, local run of sample app, basic auth validation
- Week 2: Embedding pilot, reranker test, structured-output demo, internal findings doc

Next steps I'd like to confirm: 1) Can you share a short dev/staging dataset (anonymized) for the embedding test? 2) Are there any network constraints (firewalls, proxy) we should know about for running the sample against your environment? 3) Which day next week is best for a 60-minute demo (I propose Tue 2027-04-20 or Thu 2027-04-22 afternoon PT).

Attachments: integration-worksheet.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx, redwood-sdk-sample-app.zip (small sample with both Python and TS quickstarts).

Thanks — happy to adjust based on what you need.

--
Alex Martinez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sara Patel <sara@dataco.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T18:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call architectural worksheet + SDK sandbox next steps

Alex — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset: We can provide a de-identified sample of our ticket corpus (CSV, ~30k rows). I'll push to a secure S3 link by Monday.
- Network: We have a strict outbound proxy; we may need to test the SDK through the proxy or use a private deployment.
- Auth: Security will require we see how API keys look and whether tokens can be short-lived.

One ask: for the structured output/tool-calling demo, can you show both the LLM calling an internal webhook and producing a structured JSON payload we can validate? That's a critical ask from our devs.

I'll confirm the demo slot after I check calendars; favoring Thu 4/22 afternoon PT.

Thanks,
Sara
Director, Product Integrations
DataCo
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T19:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Post-call architectural worksheet + SDK sandbox next steps (DataCo)

Team — forwarding Sara's reply. Can you weigh in on the following: 

- Proxy / network path: best approach for a quick POC? We can either: (A) show SDK behind customer proxy by providing proxy env vars in the sample app, or (B) spin a short-lived dedicated staging host in our cloud to avoid their outbound policy. Which is lower-friction?
- Structured output: Karthik, can we prepare a small tool-calling example that materializes a create_ticket JSON and verifies schema?
- Embeddings scale/compute: Marcus, rough estimate for running embeddings on 30k rows (deid) for an initial rerank — GPU hours and expected cost ballpark?

I'll draft the demo agenda once you confirm.

--
Alex
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T21:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call architectural worksheet + SDK sandbox next steps (DataCo)

Short answers from my side: 

- Proxy: (A) is easiest for the customer to validate quickly — sample app can accept HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars and we include a troubleshooting note. (B) is more work operationally and requests procurement sign-off. Recommend (A) first.

- Structured output/tool-calling: I'll prepare a minimal example that does the following during the demo: 1) LLM generates a structured payload {"create_ticket": {"title":..., "priority":...}}; 2) sample webhook endpoint (local/Ngrok) validates the payload and returns a confirmation; 3) show a unit test that asserts the schema. I'll drop the sample in the repo under /examples/tool_calling/.

- Python/TS quickstarts: I'll include both a short README and a one-command start (python -m venv; pip install -r requirements.txt; REDWOOD_API_KEY=... python run_sample.py) and equivalent for TS (npm i; npm run start).

Marcus — please add embedding compute estimate below when you have a sec.

-Karthik
Senior Applied Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T08:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call architectural worksheet + SDK sandbox next steps (DataCo)

Quick estimate for 30k de-identified rows (text avg ~200 tokens):
- Embedding compute: ~30k embedding calls; with batching we can run on a single A10 / RTX6000-equivalent for ~2–3 hours.
- Cost (hosted inference): roughly $60–$120 in compute token/embedding costs for the pilot (ballpark — depends on model and batch size).
- If the customer wants on-prem/dedicated, resource reqs: 8–16GB GPU memory per card (we can propose quantized model to reduce to lower-profile cards).

I'll attach a short cost/infra note to the shared Drive.

-Marcus
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Proxy: We'll include proxy env var instructions in the quickstart and a fallback path (Ngrok) for the webhook demo.
- Auth: we'll show both short-lived API keys and an OAuth flow mock for dev. For production SAML we can scope that in the Dedicated conversation.
- Structured output/tool-calling: Karthik's preparing a demo that will both POST a structured JSON payload to a local webhook and include an automated verification step. We'll also include a small TypeScript sample that consumes the same webhook.
